correctness.rationale: For width one, the generating regular odd-gon has circumradius 1/(2 cos(pi/(2n))). Each curved addition is exactly a unit circular sector minus an isosceles triangle. Sector and triangle area, first moment, and polar second moment are integrated exactly; translating the segment from its arc center to the dihedral center supplies the R^2 area term and the first-moment cross term. Adding the exact polar moment of the generating polygon and simplifying proves the displayed J_n formula. Dihedral rotational symmetry forces scalar covariance, so the isotropic-constant formula follows algebraically. The bundled checker reconstructs all moments symbolically and verifies independent radial integrals.
risks: The published all-n area formula is used only as a comparison and is also independently reconstructed in the package.
Numerical radial integration is diagnostic only; it does not replace the symbolic proof.

value.rationale: Regular Reuleaux odd-gons are the canonical finite-arc constant-width approximants to the disk and recur as extremizers in the classical Reuleaux literature. Polar second moment is a natural mechanical and probabilistic invariant, while the isotropic constant is its affine-normalized convex-geometric form. The theorem evaluates both for the entire regular family and reveals a structural cancellation: raw inertia has a second-order disk defect but the normalized isotropic defect starts only at fourth order.
risks: The theorem is an exact family evaluation, not an extremal theorem over irregular Reuleaux polygons.
